floor_history.headline: recon: floor=2 is pure sched1 lbu-emission-order swap in FALSE-color branch; regs+opcodes identical, only [b,r,g] vs [r,g,b]; statement-reorder KILLED
s2 structural: struct-cast, walking-pointer, ternary-hoist, block-local-split all KILLED at floor=2; two-block lbu structure is load-bearing (cannot consolidate)

s3 structural: named-intermediate rg, block-local cp, and function-scope cp all KILLED at floor=2 (function-scope cp regressed to 15); CSE/copy-prop collapse leaves sched1 dependence DAG untouched, ch

frontier.hypothesis: Reuse the EXISTING function-scope local `v` (currently written only in the TRUE arm) as the OR-tree intermediate in the FALSE arm: `v = (r<<16) | (g<<8); gnd_load_tex(b | v);`. Differs from block-local `rg` only in LUID (v was declared at function-top alongside b/r/g), so the fold behavior may differ if combine treats v's cross-arm write as escape-inhibiting.
frontier.mechanism: A local written in BOTH arms of the if/else has a merged live range at the join point (or in this case a pre-existing decl). If GCC's combine treats v's cross-arm assignments as an escape barrier that prevents folding the FALSE arm's SET into the outer OR, `v = ...` would materialize as a distinct RTL SET and re-alter sched1's dependence structure.
frontier.next_probe: Edit FALSE arm to `v = (r<<16) | (g<<8); gnd_load_tex(b | v);`; sandbox. If score changes at all (up or down), the cross-arm decl matters and the axis is worth extending; if inert (score=2, emission [r,g,b] unchanged), CSE won.

frontier.hypothesis: The FALSE arm's diff is not driven by structure at all but by REGISTER-CLASS drift at BB entry: on FALSE-branch entry, target's live-in set has specific registers occupied differently than our build's, and sched1 backward-scheduling with different available-register pressure orders the ready list [b,r,g] vs [r,g,b] as a pressure-sensitive tie-break. Fix would be upstream — an outer-function edit that changes what registers are live at 80041798.
frontier.mechanism: sched1's ready-list tie-break can be pressure-sensitive when moving an insn earlier would spill a callee-save; the tie between r's chain-4 and b's chain-2 is fixed but the ORDER within priority-equals-K can hinge on which base register is unpinnable at that cycle.
frontier.next_probe: Read cc1 -da .greg dump for gnd_init_80041688 (BB2_ALLOC_DEBUG + BB2_SCHED_DEBUG) at the FALSE-block entry; enumerate hard-reg live-in set for target vs build. If they differ, the lever is in the code BEFORE the FALSE branch (post-func_800486FC arg cleanup, loop2 exit register recycling). Restructure the code between the loops and the else-arm to change what's live-in at 15cc without touching arithmetic.

frontier.hypothesis: Original source made b's lbu HIGHER-priority than r/g by declaring b's load through a distinct-type pointer that produces a fundamentally different RTL insn (not `(mem:QI (plus reg K))` but e.g. `(mem:QI (reg))` after pre-adjusted base), so that combine cannot fuse it with the OR chain and its dependency chain length is COMPUTED as longer.
frontier.mechanism: sched.c's INSN_PRIORITY walk credits a chain link per intermediate USE that combine failed to eliminate. If the b lbu has an extra insn between load and consume (e.g. an explicit `(subreg:SI ...)` widen that combine can't fold), its chain becomes length 3 tying with r/g's length 4 minus one, plus tie-break puts b first.
frontier.next_probe: Try `b = (s32)*((u8*)player + 0x1A);` with an explicit intermediate SI-mode variable holding the widened byte: `s32 bw = *(u8*)((u8*)player + 0x1A); ... gnd_load_tex(bw | ((r<<16)|(g<<8)));`. Compare with the s3 rg experiment — probably folds the same way — but if not, examine cc1 dump for a preserved (zero_extend) node.
